_readme: Redpoint Ventures (PRO-90) calibration sets, COLLECTION.md 4. Both sets were assembled and committed BEFORE any verdict or entry_stage wrote. membership_traps gates the grind at zero false members at high confidence; stage_golden is measured blind through the production protocol and decides the evidence order the grind uses, by scoring each candidate layer (the CMS `stage` reference field, the CMS excerpt sentence, the Form D band) against the key.

membership_traps._note: 20 rows, pre-registered before the grind. The dominant trap class on this investor is the HOMONYM: the Form D roster sweep returned 857 accessions across 243 issuers for 'CHRISTOPHER MOORE' alone, 105 for 'JEFFREY MILLER', 83 for 'GREG/GREGORY MARTIN' and 59 for 'MICHAEL COHEN' — four of the commonest names in American business, all real Redpoint people. The second class is investor-specific and is the reason decisions.md D5 exists: the firm's own 2000-2006 site carried a second labelled table, 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners', listing the founding partners' Brentwood and IVP book, and three of those names are on the firm's live site today. Expected verdicts were written from the filing dates against the roster tenure windows and from the firm's own contemporaneous classification, before any verdict wrote. GATE: zero false members at high confidence.

decisions.md D5. The firm's own 2000-2006 site lists Netflix under 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners', and the live site's own excerpt dates the partnership to 'their Series B in 1998' — a year before Redpoint Ventures existed. The position was Geoff Yang's at IVP; T2 and T4 put it out. The trap is that the LIVE site claims it.

decisions.md D5. In 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners' on the firm's own 2000-2006 pages; TiVo IPO'd in September 1999, before Redpoint's first fund closed, so no Redpoint fund could have taken a venture entry. On the live site today — the same trap as Netflix.

decisions.md D5. Listed under 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners'; Geoff Yang's own bio names Juniper among 'the firm's investments' at IVP, before founding Redpoint. Not in the base as a separate row is also acceptable; if present it is not_member.
In the firm's own CURRENT investments table continuously 2001-2012 across two site eras, with description, location and status. Site listing suffices (COLLECTION.md 1).
Current-investments table 2002-2009 plus the firm's own dated announcements of the 2001 Series B and 2003 Series D.
Current-investments table from 2005; the live CMS carries the entry claim ('their Series A in 2005') and the Specific Media exit.

The counter-trap: a 'Greg Martin' Form D name match that IS the firm's deal. 2tor (later 2U) is on the firm's own listing from 2010 and the live CMS names the Series A entry in 2009. A homonym rule that kills this row is too aggressive.
Live CMS plus the firm's own Medium memo 'Why Redpoint invested in Snowflake in early 2014'; Redpoint led the $26M Series B (TechCrunch, 2014-10-21).

stage_golden._note: 34 rows, pre-registered before the grind, spread across all five site eras and all four stage buckets. Two key sources, marked per row. (a) THE FIRM'S OWN DATED ANNOUNCEMENT ARCHIVE — 1,767 dated items in the live Sanity CMS, of which 318 have funding-shaped titles and 44 name both a round and a base company (sources/web/announcements.json). This is a different artefact from the layers under test: the company card's `stage` reference field and the excerpt's 'We first partnered for their Series X in YYYY' sentence. (b) EXTERNAL PRESS, web-verified in this run on 2026-09-06. The independence caveat is recorded rather than hidden: (a) is the same firm, so it scores the CMS fields honestly but cannot itself be scored against this key — the announcement layer's own score is reported only over the (b) rows. Taxonomy: Series B and later are Growth.
